_comment: Hand-maintained mapping from Eden AI's public model list to pricing.json entries.
It picks UPSTREAMS, not models. Which models each upstream offers is Eden's
business and changes week to week; following that is the whole point of this job.
A model Eden adds is published on the next run, one it drops is dropped, and both
show up as + / - lines in the run summary and the commit.
There is no hand-written model list, and there must not be one. Eden states the
model id itself, in `id`, so nothing needs translating by hand. An earlier version
of this file pinned all 103 ids; the only thing that achieved was failing the
weekly job -- and blocking 102 correct prices -- the first time Eden retired a
single model.
Eden AI is an AGGREGATOR. The prices are what Eden charges to forward a call,
which is NOT the price of calling that provider directly. providers.edenai is not
a cross-check of providers.mistral or providers.ovh.
Currency is USD. There is no currency field in the API. Confirmed by comparison
with the rendered page: the endpoint states 0.0000004 per token for
mistral/mistral-medium-2508, and https://app.edenai.run/models shows that model at
"$0.40" under a column headed "Input $".
Prices arrive per single token and are published per million, converted through
Decimal -- a plain float multiply publishes 0.39999999999999997 for $0.40.
Deliberately NOT published, though the API states them: tiered prices
(input_cost_per_token_above_128k_tokens and the _above_200k_tokens variants),
because a price that depends on context length has no representation in this
schema; search_context_cost_per_query, itself an object of three sizes; and
output_cost_per_reasoning_token / citation_cost_per_token.
Last verified against the endpoint by a human: 2026-08-17.
